notes:
Net map (traced from the ink at 7-30x; the drawing is skewed a few degrees, so
"horizontal" rails drift ~5 px down from left to right).
0 = bottom rail: GND 5 (attached at (303,376) by a short drop off the rail) and
    GND 12 (right of V-DC 6, reached by the drop at x~433 from the V-DC right
    lead). The rail runs from V-AC 3 bottom (x~59,y~364) right through V-AC 2
    bottom (x~129), the source of MOSFET-N 11 (x~274,y~372, filled dot), the GND
    5 tap (x~303), the open-circle junction under the source of MOSFET-P 4
    (x~334,y~380), the open-circle junction under I-AC 1 (x~435,y~393) and ends
    at the filled square under I-AC 0 (x~489,y~394).
n1 = top supply rail at y~121-126: V-DC 6 "+" (left) terminal, top of Zener 14
    (the rail turns down at (80,121) and runs to the zener cathode bar at
    y~184), drain of MOSFET-P 7 (filled dot at (167,124)) and drain of MOSFET-N
    8 (filled dot at (289,125)).
n2 = zener/bias rail at y~251: anode (bottom) of Zener 14 and top of V-AC 3 meet
    at the filled dot (66,250); the rail runs right through the filled dot
    (133,252) that takes the gate of MOSFET-P 7 up at x~137, hops under the
    x~213-227 vertical (see judgment call b) and ends at x~265 where it turns up
    into the gate plate of MOSFET-N 13.
n3 = left gate line: top of V-AC 2 goes up to y~277 and right to the filled dot
    (212,276); from that dot one branch runs up (hopping the y~210 and y~252
    rails) to y~177 and then right to the gate plate of MOSFET-N 8 at x~272; the
    other branch runs down x~210 to y~330 and right to the gate plate of
    MOSFET-N 11 at x~262.
n4 = mid rail at y~209-213: source of MOSFET-P 7 (drops from the symbol at
    x~164 to y~209), source of MOSFET-N 8 (filled dot at (286,212)), drain (top
    lead) of MOSFET-N 13 (short hook up from (274,225) to the same dot), and the
    top lead of MOSFET-P 9 (the rail turns down at x~399 to y~227 and enters the
    symbol). The rail hops the x~220 vertical at (222,210).
n5 = filled dot at (278,290): source (bottom lead) of MOSFET-N 13 dropping at
    x~279, drain (top lead) of MOSFET-N 11, and the left end of Resistor 10.
n6 = filled dot at (341,294): right end of Resistor 10, source of MOSFET-P 9
    (down x~394 to y~267, left to x~342, down to the dot), and the top lead of
    MOSFET-P 4 (up at x~338).
n7 = gate of MOSFET-P 9 -> right at y~252 to x~491 -> down at x~504 to the top
    of I-AC 0. Two terminals only, nothing else on the run.
n8 = gate of MOSFET-P 4 -> right at y~355 to x~386 -> up to y~297 -> right to
    x~434 -> down to the top of I-AC 1. Two terminals only.

Judgment calls:
(a) Crossings vs junctions. Junctions in this drawing are drawn either as a
    heavy filled dot (all of (66,250), (133,252), (167,124), (212,276),
    (286,212), (278,290), (289,125), (341,294)) or, along the bottom rail, as a
    small OPEN circle where a lead drops onto it ((334,380) under MOSFET-P 4 and
    (435,393) under I-AC 1) / a small filled square ((489,394) under I-AC 0).
    I read the open circles as junctions: in each case a single lead terminates
    there on the rail (a T, not a 4-way crossing), so there is nothing for a hop
    to avoid, and reading them as breaks would strand I-AC 0, I-AC 1 and
    MOSFET-P 4 with no return path.
(b) The vertical carrying n3 from (221,177) down to (212,276) crosses BOTH the
    n4 mid rail (at y~210) and the n2 bias rail (at y~252). Checked at 22-30x:
    each crossing is a drawn semicircular hop bulging to the right (the lower one
    is a large unmistakable semicircle; the upper one is a tighter but clearly
    rounded right-hand detour), and neither carries a dot. So these are
    CROSSINGS, not junctions: n3 stays separate from n4 and n2. This is also the
    only reading that leaves MOSFET-N 8 and MOSFET-N 11 with a gate drive
    distinct from their own drain/source nodes.
(c) MOSFET orientation. 7, 8, 11 and 13 are drawn with the gate plate on the
    LEFT and the three channel leads exiting right; 4 and 9 are mirrored (gate
    plate on the RIGHT, channel leads exiting left). In every one of the six the
    middle (bulk-arrow) lead is tied to the far lead from the top one, i.e. bulk
    is tied to the lower channel terminal, so each symbol contributes only three
    distinct nets.
(d) Drain/source assignment. Terminal order used is [drain, gate, source] with
    index 0 = the upper channel lead and index 2 = the lower channel lead for
    every MOSFET (the lower lead is the one nearer ground in all six). For the
    three MOSFET-P symbols (4, 7, 9) the physical source would arguably be the
    upper lead, but swapping indices 0 and 2 does not change the net partition,
    and this keeps the file internally consistent.
(e) V-DC 6 is drawn with "+" inside the left half of the circle, so index 0
    (left) = n1 and index 1 (right) = 0 via GND 12.
(f) Zener 14: cathode bar on top (lead up to the n1 rail), anode triangle below
    (lead down to n2). Terminal 0 = cathode/top, 1 = anode/bottom.
(g) Long pencil dropouts. The y~212 rail has a ~14 px gap in the ink between
    x=326 and x=340 and the y~252 gate run of MOSFET-P 9 has a ~10 px gap
    between x=446 and x=456. Both were checked at 20x: the surviving fragments
    are collinear at the same y and the gaps are binarisation dropout of the
    same faint stroke, so each is treated as one continuous wire.
(h) Tier-2 simcheck finding, kept deliberately: nets n7 and n8 have NO DC PATH
    TO GROUND. Each consists of exactly one AC current source terminal and one
    MOSFET gate, both open at DC. The ink is unambiguous here - I-AC 0's top
    lead runs to the gate of MOSFET-P 9 and touches nothing else, and I-AC 1's
    top lead runs to the gate of MOSFET-P 4 and touches nothing else - so this
    is a real property of the drawing (a legitimate small-signal/AC arrangement),
    not a mis-trace. No other Tier 1 or Tier 2 fault.
